metadata.title: One Tool a Week.
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon: Swedish, one word. Narrator Yatra, own channel (@Yatra), Kokoro af_bella. Per the human's instruction the SPOKEN open begins 'Hi, I'm Yatra' at B00 rather than deferring the self-introduction to beat two.
metadata.color_semantics: ONE terracotta #D97757 event per beat. It marks the actionable or the unfinished: the tool link, the article title rule, the 'proposed not started' status. Never used to dress a claim.
metadata.note: GENRE: weekly recap on the ai-explainer chassis. HONESTY (hard, per the human): tool descriptions and article summaries stay EXACTLY at the level supplied. Brandy = 'a brand-audit tool'; Ogilvy = 'an AI copywriting coach'. NO invented audit findings, NO invented coaching outcomes, NO stats. Article titles are PARTIAL as supplied and render verbatim with their ellipses. The fashion team is PROPOSED, never described as underway.
metadata.reformat: center-cut, focus-aware; pantry/<bid>-916.* is the human replacement slot; -916 overrides honored

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Yatra. Every week I pick one AI tool from Humanitarians AI, use it properly, and write up what actually happened. This is the recap for this week — and the tool was Brandy.

Terracotta send arms — the ONE accent
Three result lines stagger in — the ask lands ANSWERED

output: this week's tool: Brandy — brand audit
shipped: one LinkedIn post, two Substack articles

beats.narration_text: Here's the shape of the series, and why it might be useful to you. One tool a week, used on something real, then written up honestly — never reviewed from the outside. This video is the week's recap: what the tool is, what I wrote about it, and what's coming next.

beats.narration_text: The first article is called 'I Ran Our Own Brand Audit Tool On…' — and the answer to that sentence is us. I pointed Brandy at Humanitarians AI itself and wrote up what it surfaced. Auditing your own brand with your own tool is the honest version of a demo.

beats.narration_text: The second article is about a different Humanitarians AI tool — Ogilvy, an AI copywriting coach. The piece is called 'I Told an AI Copywriting Coach I…' and it's about what happened when I actually took the coaching. Same method as Brandy: use it for real, then report.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. If you build or market something, paste this: audit my own product with my own tool, then tell me what I'd have to admit publicly if I published the result. Then check whether it names something you'd rather not write about. That's usually the article worth writing.
